evidence_items.explanation: The paper establishes a related financial incentive under its model and tests open models. Misreporting tokenization differs from generating unnecessary tokens, and the experiments do not establish either named provider's actual economics.

evidence_items.locator: Working with Claude Opus 5, Wade Foster testimonial
evidence_items.explanation: Anthropic publishes a customer report of improved performance without more tokens. This weighs against treating token billing as proof of inefficient design, but does not eliminate a possible conflicting incentive.

evidence_items.locator: Section How our agentic harness streamlines repeated work
evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI describes engineering measures that reduce repeated computation and context overhead. These are relevant counterevidence to an automatic link from token billing to inefficient design, but are not an independent measure of incentives.

evidence_items.locator: Section How we advance the efficiency frontier
evidence_items.explanation: The disclosure combines token-metered pricing with claimed efficiency gains and lower customer prices. It does not disclose the marginal profit from unnecessary tokens.

unresolved_gaps: No matched marginal serving-cost and revenue data establish the return from unnecessary tokens for both providers.
The research concerns a related billing manipulation, not the asserted model-design mechanism.
Public efficiency claims do not independently establish design incentives or their relative strength.
Customer retention, competition, and differences between API and subscription incentives remain unmeasured.
